{{Short description|German physicist}}
{{Orphan|date=February 2022}}

'''Sylvia Speller''' was born on June 17, 1967, in [[Haren, Germany|Haren]], [[Germany]]. She is a German [[physicist]] who obtained her [[Dr. rer. nat.]] from the [[Osnabrück University|University of Osnabruck]] (1995) and has been a [[professor]] in the faculty of mathematics and natural sciences at the [[University of Rostock]] since 2012. She teaches and researches experimental physics, specifically, surface and interface physics, [[nanophysics]], and scanning probe methods. Speller is currently a member of the [[German Physical Society]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Speller, Sylvia - Catalogus Professorum Rostochiensium|url=http://cpr.uni-rostock.de//resolve/id/cpr_person_00003300|access-date=2022-01-29|website=cpr.uni-rostock.de}}</ref>

== Education ==
After gaining her [[Abitur]] in Haren, Germany, she proceeded to attend the [[University of Osnabruck]] (1986–1992) where she studied [[physics]]. In 1995, she was awarded a [[Dr. rer. nat.]] by the [[Osnabrück University|University of Osnabruck]], where she worked as a [[research associate]] (1992–1995). She continued her academic career as a [[Postdoctoral researcher|postdoc]] and a [[scientific assistant]] (research fellow) at [[Eindhoven University of Technology|TU Eindhoven]] in the Netherlands, University of Osnabruck, and finally the [[Katholieke Universiteit Leuven|University of Leuven]] in [[Belgium]] until 2001. She was then appointed as the full professor of experimental physics at the [[Radboud University Nijmegen|Radboud University]] in [[Nijmegen]], [[Netherlands]], until 2012.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prof. Dr. Sylvia Speller - AG Oberflächen- und Grenzflächenphysik - Universität Rostock |url=https://www.psi.physik.uni-rostock.de/prof-dr-sylvia-speller/ |access-date=2024-05-28 |website=www.psi.physik.uni-rostock.de}}</ref> Finally, she became a professor at the University of Rostock, where she currently teaches and studies.<ref name=":0"/>

== Teaching and research areas ==
Speller works with surface and interface physics, [[nanophysics]], and scanning probe methods.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Faculty Profile on the University of Rostock|url=http://cpr.uni-rostock.de//resolve/id/cpr_person_00003300}}</ref> Surface and interface physics<ref>{{Cite book|title=Solid Surfaces, Interfaces and Thin Films {{!}} SpringerLink|series=Graduate Texts in Physics|year=2015|url=https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/978-3-319-10756-1.pdf|language=en-gb|doi=10.1007/978-3-319-10756-1|isbn=978-3-319-10755-4 }}</ref> are sub-disciplines of solid state physics. Interface physics is the study of the small atomic layers that separate two distinct, and intimately connected, surfaces. By extension, surface physics seeks to better understand surfaces, a very simple type of interface, at an atomic level. Both of these niches are utilized primarily to analyze research questions regarding nanoscience, corrosion and catalysts research. Scanning probe methods, more commonly known as scanning probe microscopy, is a study centered around the tools used to make images of nanoscale structures and surfaces, like atoms.<ref>{{Cite web|title=NanoTeachers - Bringing Nanoscience into the classroom|url=https://teachers.stanford.edu/|access-date=2022-02-18|website=teachers.stanford.edu}}</ref>

Speller has made contributions to medical research and has been cited in numerous books. In some of her most recent work, focused on combatting shortcomings within the field of [[Implant (medicine)|medical implantology]], she sought to find a better design for longterm, tissue-integrated implants.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Gruening|first1=Martina|last2=Dawson|first2=Jonathan E.|last3=Voelkner|first3=Christian|last4=Neuber|first4=Sven|last5=Fricke|first5=Katja|last6=van Rienen|first6=Ursula|author6-link=Ursula van Rienen|last7=Speller|first7=Sylvia|last8=Helm|first8=Christiane A.|last9=Nebe|first9=J. Barbara|date=January 2021|title=Automatic Actin Filament Quantification and Cell Shape Modeling of Osteoblasts on Charged Ti Surfaces|journal=Applied Sciences|language=en|volume=11|issue=12|pages=5689|doi=10.3390/app11125689|issn=2076-3417|doi-access=free}}</ref> Outside of her personal academic achievements, Speller has been cited in several books including ''Laser Ablation and Desorption'' and ''Nano-society: Pushing the Boundaries of Technology.'' Her work as a researcher has been useful in advancing knowledge across a variety of fields and disciplines.{{citation needed|date=April 2022}}
